paper_metadata.title: Data is often loadable in short depth: Quantum circuits from tensor networks for finance, images, fluids, and proteins

experiments.description: AMLET tensor-network-based amplitude-encoding state preparation evaluated on finance time-series data (stock indices) across multiple qubit sizes and depth layers.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical vectors of minute-by-minute stock index values are loaded into n qubits with length M = 2^n.

problem_instance.description: Minute-by-minute financial time-series loading for stock indices.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Huge stock price data: Intraday minute bar

dataset_specification.description: Stock indices: S&P 500, Nikkei 225, DAX 30, EUROSTOXX; minute-by-minute data; trading-hours-only data with discontinuities between days.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Data recorded only during trading hours; vectors normalized for state preparation; quality measured on unnormalized vectors with epsilon = 1 currency unit.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Circuit depth required to satisfy the finance error criterion was evaluated across qubit counts; results summarized over the dataset with reported range/standard deviation of depths.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Tensor-network decomposition via repeated SVD, truncation, tensor expansion, fusing/splitting/reindexing, and contraction to produce a quantum circuit.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Circuit concatenation across layers; evaluation of approximation error against the original financial vector.

convergence_data.variance_across_runs: small range/standard deviation of depths reported for financial data

results.unit: O(M) for bounded depth using naive matrix routines

speedup_claims.factor: orders of magnitude lower depth than general loading algorithm
speedup_claims.conditions: for the tested real-world datasets; especially at 12 and 16 qubits
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports depth comparisons rather than runtime speedups; exact factor depends on dataset and qubit count.
Reduction is reported for AMLET relative to the layer-by-layer method.

speedup_claims.factor: exponential depth avoided in many practical cases
speedup_claims.conditions: general amplitude encoding without ancilla qubits
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a general statement about state preparation complexity, not a measured benchmark.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M) for bounded depth using naive matrix routines; SVD-based construction scales at most linearly in vector length M for constant number of layers.

experiments.description: AMLET tensor-network-based amplitude-encoding state preparation evaluated on image data from the Intel Image Classification dataset.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-dimensional RGB images encoded in row-major format with all red values listed before all blue values; compressed to 14 qubits.

problem_instance.description: Image loading for the Intel Image Classification dataset.

dataset_specification.description: Six categories including buildings and forests; images compressed to 14 qubits; row-major RGB encoding.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compression to 14-qubit representation; row-major RGB grouping.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Approximate images were visually inspected; figure shows results for D = 1 to 4 and notes the poorest-fidelity images in each class.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Tensor-network decomposition via repeated SVD, truncation, tensor expansion, fusing/splitting/reindexing, and contraction to produce a quantum circuit.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Approximate image reconstruction and visual comparison to original images.

speedup_claims.factor: short-depth loading with D = 1 through 4 shown
speedup_claims.conditions: for selected Intel Image Classification samples compressed to 14 qubits
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper provides qualitative image reconstructions and depth examples, not a numeric accuracy table.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M) for bounded depth using naive matrix routines; SVD-based construction scales at most linearly in vector length M for constant number of layers.

experiments.description: AMLET tensor-network-based amplitude-encoding state preparation evaluated on turbulent fluid velocity data.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Incompressible turbulent velocity data encoded using only the velocity component along the direction of bulk flow.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Error criterion based on bounded CI and conservation of total momentum within tolerance.

problem_instance.description: Turbulent fluid velocity loading from a curated dataset.
problem_instance.dataset_name: A curated dataset for data-driven turbulence modelling

dataset_specification.description: Incompressible turbulent velocity data; only the bulk-flow velocity component Ur encoded.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Selected only Ur; enforced momentum-conservation criterion and bounded CI.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Circuit depth required to satisfy fluid error criteria was evaluated across qubit counts; anomalous depth jumps attributed to error cancellation.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Tensor-network decomposition via repeated SVD, truncation, tensor expansion, fusing/splitting/reindexing, and contraction to produce a quantum circuit.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Approximate velocity reconstruction and momentum-error evaluation.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit classical baseline or speedup comparison is reported for the fluid dataset in the provided text.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M) for bounded depth using naive matrix routines; SVD-based construction scales at most linearly in vector length M for constant number of layers.

experiments.description: AMLET tensor-network-based amplitude-encoding state preparation evaluated on protein atomic position data from large Protein Data Bank entries.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Protein atomic coordinates encoded as vectors of three-coordinate positions; non-overlapping atom sequences loaded for each qubit count.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: RMSD threshold used as the accuracy criterion.

problem_instance.description: Protein atomic position loading for large proteins from the Protein Data Bank.

dataset_specification.description: Large proteins related to ribosome function, HIV-1 capsid, and protein translation; includes some atoms from RNA molecules; non-overlapping atom sequences used to create larger datasets for each qubit count.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Loaded non-overlapping sequences of atoms; evaluated RMSD against exact atomic positions.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Circuit depth required to satisfy RMSD criterion was evaluated across qubit counts; scalability discussed up to 20,000 atoms and extrapolated to titin.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Tensor-network decomposition via repeated SVD, truncation, tensor expansion, fusing/splitting/reindexing, and contraction to produce a quantum circuit.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Approximate protein coordinate reconstruction and RMSD evaluation.

speedup_claims.conditions: for the largest known protein (titin) if the observed trend persists
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an extrapolation, not a measured result.

speedup_claims.factor: far shallower than general amplitude encoding
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the depths are far shallower but does not provide a single numeric speedup factor.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(M) for bounded depth using naive matrix routines; SVD-based construction scales at most linearly in vector length M for constant number of layers.
